newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian spy hotline a success, and that's official.
newsitem.headline: Russian spy hotline a success, and that's official.

text.p: The head of Russian counter-intelligence said on Tuesday his public offer to Russians spying for foreign powers to call a special hotline and become double agents was yielding some surprising results.
"When I tell you the results, you will be stunned," General Nikolai Kovalyov, head of the Federal Security Service (FSB), the successor to the Soviet-era KGB, said in televised remarks.
He said he had been hoping for at least one telephone call but the number of callers was counted in double digits. Kovalyov did not give details.

The unorthodox offer made by the FSB earlier this month appeared to be a sign the old KGB was adapting to the new market economy. The FSB says foreign intelligence activity has never subsided in Russia despite the end of the Cold War.
Kovalyov's remarks came one day after Earl Pitts, a 13-year FBI veteran and counter-intelligence expert, was sentenced to 27 years in prison for selling U.S. national security documents to Moscow.

The FSB says over the past six months alone the service had caught 11 foreign agents and thwarted 39 attempts to send secret information abroad. It says it caught 39 Russian agents of foreign powers in 1995 and 1996 and 400 foreign spies.
